title: Chicken or turkey and noodles with gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of boiled chicken or turkey served with noodles and a thick gravy. The meat is steamed or boiled, then sliced, while the noodles are made from wheat flour. The gravy is usually prepared from broth, flour and spices, giving the meal a rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed white meats worldwide.
Egg or wheat noodles are common in traditional dishes across many cultures.
A broth‑based gravy increases the bioavailability of nutrients from the meat.
The dish is often served in school cafeterias because it is easy to digest and protein‑rich.
In some regions vegetables (carrots, peas) are added to boost nutritional value.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat (especially turkey)
items.content: White meat contains less saturated fat than red meat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals – iron and zinc
items.content: Iron from poultry is highly absorbable, and zinc is important for immune health.

items.title: Carbohydrates from noodles provide energy
items.content: Wheat noodles supply a quick source of glucose needed for physical activity.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Gluten in noodles
items.content: Traditional wheat noodles contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing chicken or turkey pieces with noodles and drizzling the gravy over them. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) or lightly sautéed vegetables for added flavor and color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers within 2 hours of cooking, place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil to destroy any possible bacteria.
